o1.biggest_strength: It answers the competitive question directly — where we lose (agencies, 60% of Semrush losses), where we don't (backlinks 64-21, keyword data a statistical tie) — and nails the numbers: blended churn 4.9%, Lite 70% of churn, usage limits about a third of all churn, 37% Lite survival at 12 months, 21,000 multi-site accounts at 42% of free-to-paid conversions.
o1.biggest_mistake: Move 5 (publish link studies, 'pick one study topic') is the closest thing to the generic content-marketing advice the owner hates, and its success metric — in-house trial share rising above 38% — is a stretch from publishing one study.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace Move 5 with a second quantified competitive lever and give every move the same one-line ranking rationale that Move 1 gets.

o2.biggest_strength: The most honest analyst in the room: every projection is a labelled range with a named assumed input ('projections, not results'), and it flags that the survey only covers SEOs who used both tools — the per-1,000-trial table and 'the competitive threat is about 9 customers per 10,000 a month' calibrate the Semrush fear properly.
o2.biggest_mistake: Its ranking contradicts its own stated rule: the enterprise pack is projected at only +3 to 7 customers per 1,000 and sits above the agency report at +13 to 26, and the headline 'first move this month' is the free-tier email track rather than the Lite limit fix the owner thinks is the fastest money.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put the Lite top-up and agency report at the top of the ranked list, call the Lite fix the fastest money by name, and keep the assumption-labelled projections exactly as they are.

reason: Both are sound and numerically clean, but Output 1 delivers the competitive answer the owner actually asked for — where we lose, where we don't, five ranked moves with owners, first steps and metrics, and an explicit what-not-to-do — while Output 2, for all its rigour, buries the agency report last and ranks a +3–7 customer enterprise pack above a +13–26 customer move.
